analysis.title: Global Macro Monthly: The Boom, the Ballot, and the Hikes
key_insights: AI investment and record US corporate profits have sustained the US expansion despite higher energy prices, rising bond yields and a renewed Fed hiking cycle. Profit growth is expected to slow in 2027.

Corporate profit share of US GDP is at its highest since the Second World War, led by technology and energy. AI capex growth is nearing its peak just as employment recovers, which points to slower earnings growth alongside further tightening.

More than 80% of estimated AI ecosystem revenues still come from recycled capex rather than customers outside the industry. Chinese open-weight models pressure token prices, and data-centre operators carry high fixed costs and growing financing commitments.

AI buildout added an estimated 0.3 percentage points to US consumer prices through energy costs and technology bottlenecks. Much of the investment spending flows overseas, so the direct contribution to US activity is smaller than headline capex suggests.

In an AI crash scenario, import intensity limits the GDP hit and the few jobs created limit labour damage. Losing an estimated 800,000 jobs would raise unemployment by about 0.5 percentage points before wider spillovers. TS Lombard still expects equity losses and credit stress to trigger a recession, with healthy private balance sheets and room for Fed easing limiting its severity. An abrupt AI collapse is not the central forecast.

AI-related products account for roughly two-thirds of Chinese export growth this year. Slower global tech demand would weaken exports but could prompt a stronger domestic policy response ahead of next year's political transition. China consumption and infrastructure equities are an alternative to the tech supply chain.

October payrolls rose 165,000, with gains in manufacturing and services. Wage growth looks to be bottoming, and immigration restrictions limit labour supply. TS Lombard's base case is quarterly Fed hikes extending beyond Q1 2027, with a terminal rate possibly higher than markets expect.

Higher energy prices and AI capex drove much of 2026's US profit growth, and both should fade in 2027. Recovering wages will raise unit labour costs and may reverse some margin expansion. TS Lombard favours rotation toward less concentrated equity exposure and economies with less advanced profit cycles, citing the UK.

Democrats swept Congress in the midterms, which weakens Trump's legislative position and raises the odds of fiscal brinkmanship. Bipartisan deals on permitting reform and some industrial policy remain possible, and Trump keeps executive authority over trade and foreign affairs. Democratic gubernatorial wins in states with much of the planned US data-centre capacity add political resistance to AI infrastructure.

Lula's re-election triggered an exceptional Brazil sell-off. TS Lombard sees the administration signalling tighter spending rules and expects a modest reform programme that averts a 2027 crisis. It calls the sell-off an attractive entry point and prefers Brazilian equities over Mexico, with continued exposure to local rates.
India: political pressure, weaker consumer sentiment and protests raise the odds of fiscal support while the RBI tries to contain price pressures.
Middle East conflict keeps oil elevated and supports expectations of higher rates. The central scenario is periodic escalation within a contained conflict, with oil eventually falling toward $80/bbl.

ECB held at 2.5% in October on limited second-round inflation evidence. Market-driven tightening has pushed real financing costs near the peaks of the last hiking cycle, and lending standards have tightened. TS Lombard expects a December hike, then a path dependent on domestic inflation and energy. Core HICP flash was steady at 2.5% in October.

France is the weakest link in European sovereign debt. Political instability and unresolved fiscal pressure leave OAT spreads exposed ahead of next year's presidential election, particularly if budget talks fail. TS Lombard says banks will offer a buying opportunity once the dust settles.

BoE raised Bank Rate 25bp to 4% in November. All nine MPC members voted to tighten and Catherine Mann wanted a larger move. TS Lombard expects one more hike to 4.25%, most likely in February, then a prolonged hold. Markets price more tightening than that, partly from inflation risk premia.

BoJ is expected to hike in December, March and July to take the policy rate to 2%. Higher domestic yields may draw portfolio flows into JGBs, supporting the yen. In a US-centred risk-off episode, unhedged JGBs could outperform Treasuries.

China: the PBoC moved its policy anchor to the 1.25% overnight reverse repo rate, effectively lowering the funding-rate floor by 15bp, and easier liquidity is likely to precede rate cuts. September exports rose 36.3% y/y, but the October export-orders PMI fell to 48.7 and the composite PMI fell to 49.7. Q3 GDP was 4.5% y/y.

Euro area growth forecast is about 1.0% in 2026 and 1.4-1.5% in 2027. German infrastructure and defence spending (€500bn infrastructure/climate programme) supports activity, while energy costs weigh. The ECB Bank Lending Survey shows tighter credit standards and weaker loan demand.
TS Lombard forecasts US 2026 inflation at 3.5% and GDP growth at 2.5%, with 2.5% growth in 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Brazilian equities relative to Mexico, with continued exposure to local Brazilian rates
trade_ideas.rationale: The post-election sell-off is an attractive entry point, and fiscal constraints give an incentive for a modest reform programme.
trade_ideas.risk: Investors doubt Lula's willingness to address fiscal imbalances, and the legislature is hostile.

trade_ideas.description: Rotate toward less concentrated equity exposure and economies with less advanced profit cycles, such as the UK
trade_ideas.rationale: Slower AI capex growth, fading energy gains and rising unit labour costs squeeze US margins in 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: An AI reversal or a renewed energy shock could hit equities broadly.

trade_ideas.description: Buy European banks once French political dust settles

trade_ideas.description: Unhedged JGBs as an alternative to Treasuries for protection in a US-centred risk-off episode

trade_ideas.description: Favour Chinese equities exposed to consumption and infrastructure over technology supply chains
trade_ideas.rationale: They offer an alternative to the tech supply chains currently benefiting from US investment.
trade_ideas.risk: Weak domestic demand and trade retaliation against China's surplus.

risk_factors: US labour-market reacceleration drives wage pressure and a higher Fed terminal rate.
Slower AI capex growth and rising unit labour costs squeeze US corporate profits.
Growing reliance on debt financing increases vulnerabilities in the AI ecosystem.
Renewed Hormuz escalation prolongs the energy shock and inflation pressure.
Higher real financing costs constrain European investment and domestic demand.
US political gridlock and French fiscal uncertainty raise policy and sovereign-market risks.
Rapid ECB tightening to 3% could weaken the euro area recovery before it takes root.
Further BoE tightening beyond TS Lombard's forecast risks suppressing an emerging UK recovery.
charts_described: Chart titled 'Payrolls 165k pop up' accompanies the discussion of October payrolls, with no levels given in the text.
vol_and_positioning: Warsh's move away from conventional forward guidance should increase market disagreement over the Fed's reaction function and raise short-term policy volatility.
Bloomberg BoE Speak Index is at hawkish levels associated with 10% CPI, while markets price more BoE tightening than TS Lombard expects.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict and Hormuz (SoH) closure risk keep oil prices elevated and complicate monetary policy.
US midterms: Democrats took control of Congress, constraining Trump's legislative agenda while leaving executive power over trade and foreign affairs.
Lula's re-election in Brazil triggered a sharp sell-off in Brazilian assets.
French political instability and fiscal uncertainty ahead of next year's presidential election pressure OATs.
Ukraine war: the potential for serious peace talks is emerging.
The US Supreme Court and other US courts struck down tariffs, which dents Trump's trade policy.
China's trade surplus in high-tech and clean-energy goods invites stronger trade retaliation, and the EU is uniting against Chinese export surges.
India: political pressure and protests complicate the inflation outlook.

tension_points.bull_case: Profits are broadening beyond technology, supporting hiring and investment, and the expansion's underlying resilience remains intact.
tension_points.bear_case: Slower AI capex growth, fading energy gains and rising unit labour costs threaten margins in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reacceleration of AI capex growth, or wage growth that stays subdued despite recovering employment.

tension_points.bull_case: Falling computing costs could stimulate enough demand to sustain revenues, and hyperscaler spending still supports earnings across the supply chain.
tension_points.bear_case: More than 80% of AI ecosystem revenue is recycled capex, Chinese open-weight models pressure token prices, and operators face high fixed costs and financing commitments.

tension_points.bull_case: Fiscal constraints give an incentive for a modest reform programme and the administration has signalled tighter spending rules.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors doubt Lula's willingness to fix fiscal imbalances, and the legislature is hostile.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to deliver the signalled spending-rule tightening.

tension_points.bull_case: No second-round effects in wages or core inflation give the ECB room to hold after a December hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Real financing costs are near the previous peak, credit demand is weakening, and fast tightening to 3% could damage the recovery.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Prolonged energy pressure would bring the 3% terminal rate forward to March.
